items.title: 66086_Zilner T. Randolph oral history interview
items.q: "when I started arranging for him... I knew he could read then."

ctx.x: He was singing all those intervals and doing this way in the chair, he was singing the intervals, and he said to me, "Randy, that's pretty. That's really a pretty tune." But we never did get a chance to record it, though. But -- and I knew right then, I went back and told my wife, I said, "They say Louie can't read music. Louie took that song and solfeged that song off." (unintelligible)? See, that's the solfeggio. I said, "He solfeged that song off direct from sight -- sight reading." And so, then I knew he…
You did write parts for him?
